PE1-07.hint: \(f^{-1}(b) = a\) means \(f(a) = b\). Find \(b\) in the \(f(x)\) row, then read the input above it.
slips: Reading \(f^{-1}(2)\) as \(f(2)\). The \(2\) is an output of \(f\), so look for it in the bottom row.
Reading \(f^{-1}(2)\) as \(\dfrac{1}{f(2)}\). The \(-1\) in \(f^{-1}\) means inverse, not reciprocal.
Reporting the output from the table instead of the input above it.
PE1-07.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-08.hint: Write \(y = f(x)\), swap \(x\) and \(y\), then solve for \(y\). In (b), collect every \(y\) term on one side so you can factor \(y\) out.
slips: Solving for \(y\) but forgetting to swap \(x\) and \(y\).
Writing \(f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{6x+11}\). The \(-1\) is not an exponent.
In (b), dividing instead of factoring when \(y\) appears in two terms.
PE1-08.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)
